consequence: Kill condition applies verbatim: the ceiling removal does NOT transfer and is scoped to the
associative-lookup family, exactly as the attribution separation was in cycle 2.
On the lookup family compaction takes adaptive halting from 0.97-1.01x to 1.60-1.95x at batch
128-256. On the streaming family it takes it from 0.83x to 1.07x -- parity, not a win.
why_it_did_not_transfer: The first anticipated failure mode named it before the run: 'at c_step = 0.3343 us a removed row
saves a third of a microsecond while a gather costs tens'. The streaming core is attention-free
and eight times cheaper per example-step than the lookup core, so compaction removes rows whose
cost is comparable to the cost of removing them.
This is the same variable the failed cost model of QNEURO3-RUNTIME-P1 identified qualitatively
while getting its numbers wrong: the ratio c_step / c_compact decides whether compaction pays.
The equation remains unclaimed; the ordering it implies was right in sign on both families.
the_boundary_this_establishes: Compaction removes the lockstep straggler ceiling when the per-step cost is large enough relative
to the compaction cost. Measured: it works at c_step = 2.66 us/example-step (1.95x at batch 256)
and does not at c_step = 0.33 us/example-step (1.07x).
This is a second boundary of the same shape as the first. The advantage of adaptive computation
is real, and every time it is measured under a stronger control it turns out to be bounded by
something that has nothing to do with the mechanism itself.
measurement_caveats: The batch-64 select timing (33.5 us/example) is anomalously fast relative to batch 32 (56.5) and
batch 128 (22.5), producing a comp-vs-select of 0.80x that does not fit the trend. Fanless
thermal variation is the likely cause. It is reported as measured; no rerun was taken, because
the frozen protocol allowed one attempt.
